record.paper_title: Quo Vadis Strangeness? Strangeness — Open Questions
record.original_question: Can normal confined hadronic matter, without invoking local color deconfinement, generate the observed strangeness enhancement and relative strange-antibaryon yields in relativistic nuclear collisions, and, if so, what additional observable physical effects would demonstrate the new confined-matter mechanism?

evidence.quote: Both these effects occur naturally in the deconfined phase. The second one has been postulated in order to generate strangeness enhancement in normal, confined hadronic matter. Within such an ad-hoc scheme the challenge for the inventor is then to demonstrate some other physical effect that would arise from such new and yet undiscovered confined hadronic matter phenomena. Perhaps equally relevant to the assessment of such proposals is the fact that one has to look for more than ‘strangeness enhancement’ with flavor observables, and in particular the (relative) yields of strange antibaryons originating in novel forms of confined matter should be also compared with the experimental data.

artifact.status_search_result: Current literature (including studies of hadronic transport models, statistical hadronization, and recent ALICE measurements of strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions) indicates that no purely confined-hadronic-matter model has been established that reproduces both the magnitude of strangeness enhancement and the relative multi-strange antibaryon hierarchy seen in A+A collisions while providing an independent distinguishing observable. Detailed-balance arguments suggest hadronic processes are insufficient to enhance strange antibaryons to QGP levels, but a definitive no-go theorem is absent. The question therefore remains open.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness and quark–gluon plasma
status_evidence.snippet: The energy needed to produce strange hadrons in a thermally equilibrated hadron gas is significantly higher than in QGP; strangeness in the plasma phase is more abundant than in the hadronic gas phase.
status_evidence.claim: Standard view is that hadronic mechanisms cannot easily match QGP-level strangeness production.

status_evidence.title: Enhanced production of multi-strange hadrons in high-multiplicity proton–proton collisions
status_evidence.snippet: ALICE observes strangeness enhancement in high-multiplicity pp collisions, challenging the traditional QGP-only interpretation.
status_evidence.claim: The mechanism for strangeness enhancement remains under active investigation; alternative confined-matter explanations are still debated.

status_evidence.title: Strangeness in strongly interacting matter
status_evidence.snippet: Hadron processes cannot enhance strange antibaryons due to detailed balance constraints, and the abundance of strange antibaryons from dynamical hadronic models is expected to be considerably smaller than obtainable in QGP models.
status_evidence.claim: Detailed-balance arguments constrain confined-matter explanations but no full no-go result is established.
